rationale: The zero-based coordinate sum of i:Fin m to Fin n lies between 0 and m(n-1), and is exactly the original one-based sum minus m. The full complex list length m(n-1)+1 and endpoints m>=3,n>=2 are retained.

Ordinary factors have one independent complex vector per mode. Symmetric factors have a complex coefficient and one repeated vector. Products use no conjugation, normalization, genericity or Vandermonde restriction.

Both width-r predicates are upward closed by padding with zero terms. Equality of their least widths therefore implies equivalence at every r; conversely the all-r equivalence gives equality by applying it at either minimum.

The relevant minima exist: ordinary tensors have coordinate-basis decompositions; Hankel tensors have symmetric finite decompositions by choosing D+1 distinct complex t values, D=m(n-1), and solving the invertible Vandermonde system h_s=sum_j c_j t_j^s, yielding vectors (1,t_j,...,t_j^(n-1)). This is a correspondence argument, not a restriction on allowed decompositions.

At r=0 both decompositions mean the zero tensor. A symmetric summand converts to an ordinary one by absorbing its scalar into one factor (m>=3 guarantees at least one factor). The zero tensor and all exceptional h are included.
The complete canonical README and ORIGINAL.md agree byte for byte. The stronger all-spectrum formula in the resolution is not imposed on the original rank-equality target.
